ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 (Public Act 2009 No 35, as amended by the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Amendment Acts 2017 and 2023); Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Code of Practice 2011 (as amended); Companies Act 1993 (Public Act 1993 No 105), ss 20–22 (name availability and reservation) and s 189 (registered office); Financial Service Providers (Registration and Dispute Resolution) Act 2008 (Public Act 2008 No 97); and the supervisory framework of the Reserve Bank of New Zealand, Financial Markets Authority and Department of Internal Affairs for AML/CFT reporting entities.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National passport office or gazetted public notary in the country of origin of the individual
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (certification by the competent Apostille authority of the country of origin) OR Consular Legalization by the New Zealand Embassy/Consulate where the origin country is not party to the Hague Apostille Convention

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry or registered agent in the corporate shareholder's jurisdiction of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization by the New Zealand diplomatic post having consular jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Applicant's corporate or retail bank, countersigned by a notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized original issued within the last 90 days; Apostille/Consular Legalization required where the bank is located in a non-Hague jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney appointing the New Zealand registered agent and corporate service provider
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Each constituent shareholder/UBO, executed before a public notary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization; the executed original must reach the New Zealand agent within its validity window

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Corporate due diligence questionnaire and beneficial ownership attestation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Applicant's ultimate beneficial owners, countersigned by the instructing counsel
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certified by counsel in the country of origin; Apostille/Consular Legalization may be required for jurisdictions designated as high-risk under FATF

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based screening of all shareholders, ultimate beneficial owners, directors and signatories against the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade (MFAT) New Zealand Sanctions Register, the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, the U.S. OFAC Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) List (mandatory for USD Fedwire and Visa/Mastercard Direct settlement rails), the UK and EU consolidated financial sanctions lists, and the New Zealand Police Financial Intelligence Unit watchlists. Politically Exposed Person (PEP) identification, including foreign PEPs, domestic PEPs assessed on a risk basis, family members and close associates, is mandatory under the AML/CFT Act 2009 and the AML/CFT (Definitions) Regulations 2011, with enhanced due diligence and senior-management approval required before onboarding any PEP-connected counterparty.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: New Zealand Companies Office — Companies Register (secure online portal: https://companies-register.companiesoffice.govt.nz)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Statutory requirement that the company name be expressed in Latin alphabetic characters, in English or Māori (including diacritics), with the compulsory suffix 'Limited' or 'Ltd' (or the Māori equivalent 'Tapui Limited' where consented to by the Registrar). Foreign-language names must be submitted in Latin-script transliteration as the primary registered name with the required English or Māori formative; a non-Latin-script version may be recorded only as a secondary trading name and must be applied for separately. The name must not be identical or almost identical to any existing reserved or registered name, must not include a restricted word without prior approval, and must not be likely to mislead under ss 20–21 Companies Act 1993.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Group (only with capitalization clarity and availability review)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Where the Registrar declines a proposed name, the written notice cites the statutory ground under ss 20–21 Companies Act 1993. The applicant may: (1) file a revised name application through the Companies Office online portal without penalty; (2) submit a written reconsideration request to the Registrar of Companies within 20 working days of the refusal notice, supported by submissions and any ministerial consents addressing the stated ground; (3) apply to the competent portfolio Minister for approval of any restricted/sensitive token contained in the name; and (4) where the final decision remains adverse, institute judicial review proceedings in the High Court of New Zealand under the Judicial Review Procedure Act 2016. A successful applicant may renew an expiring reservation solely by filing a further reservation application while the name remains unconditionally available; no statutory extension beyond the initial 20-working-day window exists without a new application.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A serviced-office or virtual physical address in New Zealand is conditionally acceptable as the registered office under s 189 Companies Act 1993, provided it is a genuine physical street address in New Zealand (not a PO Box) at which documents may be served during business hours. For the licensed payment services industry, the Financial Service Providers (Registration and Dispute Resolution) Act 2008 additionally requires a real place of business in New Zealand, and the Reserve Bank of New Zealand as AML/CFT supervisor expects local substance, accessible corporate records, and responsible-person presence; therefore, a mail-forwarding-only virtual arrangement is not compliant for an ISIC 6619 cross-border payment gateway.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk: High. Estimated probability exceeding 50% of an unannounced on-site AML/CFT inspection by the Reserve Bank of New Zealand or the Department of Internal Affairs within the first 12 months of licensing, given the High-Risk_Special_License classification of the online merchant acquiring and clearing business, the volume of cross-border transactions, and the mandatory s 129 AML/CFT Act 2009 inspection powers.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 1993 (New Zealand), ss 12 (incorporation), 14 (registration and certificate of incorporation), 16 (legal capacity), 17 (registered office), 20 (company records), 26 (constitution), 31 (company names), 35, 36, 40 and 41 (share allotment and consideration), 45, 46, 122 and 151 (director appointments and qualifications), 126, 127, 128, 131-136 and 191 (board governance and director duties), 200 (company records and register), 214-216 (registration and enforcement); Companies Regulations 1994 (prescribed forms and fees); Financial Service Providers (Registration and Disputes Resolution) Act 2008; Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009; Payment and Settlement Systems Act 2022.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE), operated electronically through the Companies Register at companies-register.companiesoffice.govt.nz.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form 2 - Application for Registration of a Company (prescribed under the Companies Regulations 1994; filed online through the Companies Register; statutory output is the Certificate of Incorporation issued under s 14 of the Companies Act 1993).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is required to incorporate an ordinary limited company under the Companies Act 1993, and no escrow deposit is mandated at incorporation. Shares may be allotted for nil or nominal consideration, provided shares are not issued at a discount. However, for a cross-border payment gateway, the board must maintain segregated settlement accounts and, if the PSP holds or controls client funds, comply with payment-network trust/escrow rules. The higher capital thresholds of the Reserve Bank of New Zealand Act 1989 (NZD 15 million for a registered bank; NZD 5 million for a non-bank deposit taker) are not engaged unless the entity elects to take deposits or operate as an authorised deposit-taking institution.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF [COMPANY] LIMITED, adopted on [date], at [registered office address], New Zealand. RESOLVED: (1) Share Capital Subscription: That the allotment of [●] ordinary shares of no par value to the subscribers named in the Application for Registration of the Company be and is hereby ratified, and the directors are authorised to receive the agreed subscription consideration in accordance with ss 35, 36, 40 and 41 of the Companies Act 1993, to issue share certificates, and to ensure that no share is allotted at a discount. (2) Registered Office: That the registered office of the Company shall be [●], New Zealand, and the address for service shall be [●]; the Company Secretary is directed to notify the Registrar, to open the office to the public during required hours, and to maintain the statutory registers and company records at that office in accordance with ss 17, 20 and 200 of the Companies Act 1993. (3) Officers and Directors: That [●] (Director ID [●]) and [●] be and are appointed as directors of the Company, that [●] be appointed Chief Executive Officer, that [●] be appointed Company Secretary, and that [●] be appointed AML/CFT Compliance Officer; each appointee has consented to act, and signed consents shall be placed in the company records and filed as required. (4) Banking and Settlement: That the Chief Executive Officer be authorised to open operating bank accounts and segregated USD settlement accounts at a New Zealand licensed bank and/or a correspondent bank with Fedwire access, and to execute account mandates, custody and payment-rail agreements necessary for the cross-border payment gateway business. (5) Statutory and Industrial Licensing: That the directors be authorised to apply for registration under the Financial Service Providers (Registration and Disputes Resolution) Act 2008, to adopt the AML/CFT compliance programme and register with the Department of Internal Affairs, and to obtain any required Visa/Mastercard third-party processor accreditation and physical premises fire/civil-defence clearances. (6) General: That the financial year end of the Company be 31 March, that the Company adopt its constitution, and that each director act in accordance with ss 131-136 of the Companies Act 1993.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office - Companies Register (online portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Run an electronic search of the Companies Register and the New Zealand Intellectual Property Office (IPONZ) trade-mark register to confirm that the proposed company name is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing name and does not contravene s 31 of the Companies Act 1993. File an online name reservation application under the selected name, providing up to three alternative names in order of preference. A successful reservation is valid for 20 working days and may be renewed once before incorporation.
required_dossiers: Proposed company name and up to three alternative names
Companies Register name availability search result
IPONZ trade-mark search result
Name reservation fee receipt
Evidence of consent from iwi or trade-mark holder if the name contains a protected or culturally sensitive term
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, file a substitute name immediately using the same reservation reference. If the Registrar rejects the name on offensive or confusingly-similar grounds, request written reasons under s 31 and submit a corrected name, or supply the written consent of the existing name holder to overcome the conflict.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation of incorporation documents, constitution and officer consents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Incorporators and licensed New Zealand registered agent / corporate solicitor
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the company constitution (optional but recommended), the consent-to-act forms for each director, the shareholder and share allotment record, the registered-office consent form, and the initial governance minutes. Conduct identity and beneficial-ownership verification on every subscriber and director to satisfy the Gatekeeper provisions of the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 before submission.
required_dossiers: Company constitution in English (if adopted) under s 26
Signed consent to act as director for each director (ss 46 and 151)
Shareholders' register and proposed share allotment schedule
Registered office address consent from the owner/lessor
AML/CFT beneficial-ownership and identity verification records
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If any consent or document is defective, correct and re-execute before filing. The incorporators may amend the draft constitution at any time prior to registration; no government appeal step applies at this preparatory stage.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Online filing of the statutory incorporation application
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office via the Companies Register
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete and submit Form 2 online, attaching the constitution and consents, selecting the share class and voting rights, nominating directors and initial shareholders, and confirming that at least one director is resident in New Zealand or Australia as permitted under s 151. Pay the statutory incorporation fee by debit/credit card or online banking. The Registrar registers the company and issues a Certificate of Incorporation if the application is in order.
required_dossiers: Form 2 - Application for Registration of a Company
Company constitution (if adopted)
Signed director consent-to-act forms
Signed registered-office consent
Name reservation reference number
Filing fee payment confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar queries the application, respond through the Companies Register portal within the stated correction period by amending particulars or supplying additional information. If registration is refused, request a written decision and seek review under the applicable provisions of the Companies Act 1993 or by judicial review in the High Court within the statutory deadline.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Certificate of Incorporation and New Zealand Business Number activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Companies / New Zealand Business Number (NZBN) Hub
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Download and retain the electronic Certificate of Incorporation. Verify the company number and the automatically allocated NZBN. Review the Companies Register extract to confirm the registered office, directors, shareholders and address for service are accurately recorded. Place the certificate, constitution, consents and share register in the statutory records at the registered office.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
NZBN registration record
Company constitution and consents
Initial share register and members' register
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate or register extract contains any error, file an electronic request for correction with the Registrar and, if necessary, submit a written application for amendment under the Companies Act 1993 supported by evidence of the correct particulars.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Inland Revenue Department tax and GST registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Inland Revenue Department (Te Tari Taake) - MyIR online portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain a New Zealand IRD number for the company. Register for GST if the company's expected 12-month taxable turnover exceeds NZD 60,000 or voluntarily if the company intends to claim GST input credits. Register for PAYE if it will employ staff, and register for resident withholding tax/non-resident withholding tax on interest, dividends and certain cross-border payments. Provide New Zealand bank account details for tax refunds.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation and NZBN
Full names, addresses and IRD numbers of all directors
Registered office and address for service
Projected turnover and GST registration worksheet
Bank account confirmation for refunds
PAYE employer registration details if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the IRD number application is delayed or queried, respond through MyIR with the confirmation of incorporation and supporting identification. If the Commissioner issues an adverse assessment or late-registration penalty, invoke the statutory dispute procedure under the Tax Administration Act 1994 by filing a Notice of Proposed Adjustment within the response period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration as a Financial Service Provider and dispute-resolution membership
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Financial Markets Authority (FMA) - Financial Service Providers Register
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Create an FSPR account and file an application registering the company as a financial service provider for the class of payment and money-transmission services, including issuing and managing means of payment and merchant acquiring/clearing services. Join an approved financial dispute resolution scheme (for example, the Financial Dispute Resolution Service Ltd) and obtain a membership certificate. Maintain the required disclosure statement and update information on the FSP Register.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation and NZBN
FSPR online application form
Approved dispute resolution scheme membership certificate
AML/CFT business risk assessment summary (abridged)
Governance chart and senior officer background details
Registered office and address for service confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If FMA queries or refuses the FSPR application, respond with supplementary documents within the specified period. If the refusal is maintained, apply for an internal reconsideration or appeal to the Financial Markets Authority Appeals Board / High Court in accordance with the Financial Service Providers (Registration and Disputes Resolution) Act 2008.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: AML/CFT compliance programme and supervisory registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Internal Affairs (Te Tari Taiwhenua) - AML/CFT Group; FMA for FSPR alignment
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare a formal business risk assessment and an AML/CFT compliance programme addressing customer due diligence, enhanced due diligence, transaction monitoring, suspicious activity reporting, sanctions screening and record keeping. Appoint a senior Compliance Officer (ordinarily a director or senior manager). Submit the programme and registration particulars to the AML/CFT supervisor. Arrange for an independent AML/CFT audit after the first two years of operation.
required_dossiers: AML/CFT Business Risk Assessment
AML/CFT Compliance Programme
Appointment letter and consent of AML/CFT Compliance Officer
Customer due diligence and enhanced due diligence procedures
Suspicious transaction and suspicious activity reporting procedures
Sanctions screening and transaction-monitoring system specification
Independent audit schedule and terms of reference
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the supervisor returns the programme for revision, amend and resubmit within 10 working days with additional risk data. If a formal direction or civil penalty is proposed, invoke the right to make written submissions and obtain legal representation in proceedings before the High Court under the AML/CFT Act.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Visa/Mastercard third-party processor or payment-facilitator accreditation and settlement-rail access
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Visa and Mastercard (scheme compliance); sponsoring New Zealand acquiring bank; Reserve Bank of New Zealand under the Payment and Settlement Systems Act 2022; Federal Reserve Fedwire network via a correspondent bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply to Visa and Mastercard, either directly as a principal third-party processor or through a licensed New Zealand acquirer/sponsor, for status as a card processor or payment facilitator for merchant acquiring and clearing. Complete and pass a PCI DSS assessment through an approved Qualified Security Assessor. Execute the applicable scheme registration and processor agreement. Establish a segregated USD settlement account at a correspondent bank with Fedwire participation and a New Zealand dollar account at a local licensed bank. Test clearing, settlement and reconciliation files before commencing live transactions.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation, FSP registration and AML/CFT registration
PCI DSS Attestation of Compliance and Report on Compliance
Detailed processing architecture and data-flow diagram
Operational risk, fraud and chargeback management manual
Recent audited financial statements
AML/CFT compliance programme and sanctions screening evidence
Segregated settlement account confirmation from the sponsoring bank or correspondent bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a card scheme refuses or delays accreditation, obtain the written non-compliance reasons, remedy the identified gaps and re-submit through the same or another sponsor. Where the sponsoring bank withdraws support, secure an alternative New Zealand licensed acquirer or apply to become a principal acquirer member if scheme capital rules are satisfied.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Physical premises, fire safety and occupational workplace clearances
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Territorial local authority (building consent authority); Fire and Emergency New Zealand (FENZ); WorkSafe New Zealand; Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Secure commercial office and/or server-hosting premises and verify the building's legal use under the Building Act 2004. Obtain a Building Warrant of Fitness (BWOF) where a compliance schedule is required, a fire evacuation scheme approval from FENZ if staff are present, an electrical certificate of compliance for computer rooms/UPS systems, and a structural load certificate for any raised floors and server racks. Implement a Health and Safety at Work Act 2015 workplace policy, hazard register and emergency-response plan.
required_dossiers: Lease or ownership evidence and local authority occupancy permit
Building Warrant of Fitness and compliance schedule
Fire Evacuation Scheme approval from Fire and Emergency New Zealand
Electrical certificate of compliance for data/network rooms
Structural load assessment for server racks and equipment areas
Health and safety policy and hazard register
Civil-defence and business-continuity plan
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a council or FENZ notice identifies non-compliance, obtain a remedial building or fire-engineer certificate, carry out the required work and request re-inspection. If the council refuses a BWOF, appeal to the relevant territorial authority hearing process or to the Building and Construction Authority under the Building Act 2004.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Financial Markets Authority (FMA) for Financial Service Provider registration; Department of Internal Affairs (Te Tari Taiwhenua) AML/CFT Group for money-transmission and payment-service supervision; Reserve Bank of New Zealand for payment-and-settlement system designation and oversight; territorial local authority and Fire and Emergency New Zealand for physical premises licensing under the Building Act 2004 and FENZ Act 2017; WorkSafe New Zealand for occupational health and safety.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Combined statutory operating licence package: (i) Financial Service Provider Registration under the Financial Service Providers (Registration and Disputes Resolution) Act 2008; (ii) AML/CFT compliance registration and approved compliance programme under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009; (iii) Visa/Mastercard Third-Party Processor or Payment Facilitator certification, with sponsoring acquirer authorisation; and (iv) physical premises building warrant of fitness and fire evacuation scheme approval.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Authority (EPA) New Zealand; territorial local authority under the Resource Management Act 1991; Ministry for the Environment for national environmental standards.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category 3 - Permitted / No Full EIA for an office-based electronic payment gateway. A formal Assessment of Environmental Effects (AEE) and resource consent under s 88 of the Resource Management Act 1991 are required only if the company undertakes building alterations, installs standby generators, constructs a data centre, or causes noise, stormwater, or hazardous-substance effects exceeding permitted-activity thresholds. No national-level Environmental Impact Assessment report is required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: For office-based electronic operations there are no point-source industrial wastewater or VOC discharge authorisations. Any domestic wastewater must comply with the local council trade-waste and sewerage bylaws. If diesel standby generators are installed, the installation must meet the National Environmental Standards for Air Quality (NES-AQ) particulate matter (PM10/PM2.5) and NOx/SOx limits, plus local noise and vibration standards. Electronic waste and UPS batteries must be disposed of through accredited e-waste and hazardous-waste facilities under the Waste Minimisation Act 2008, with records maintained for at least 7 years for AML/CFT and environmental liability purposes.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety and evacuation scheme approval from Fire and Emergency New Zealand (FENZ) under the Fire and Emergency New Zealand Act 2017; Building Warrant of Fitness under the Building Act 2004; structural load clearance for computer room raised floors and server racks; electrical certificate of compliance for high-voltage, UPS and network equipment; workplace clearance and health-and-safety induction under the Health and Safety at Work Act 2015; and a civil-defence emergency plan covering earthquake, tsunami and power-outage scenarios for continuous payment-rail availability.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue Department (Inland Revenue; Te Tari Taake) — official online portal: myIR at www.ird.govt.nz
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1 — Determine New Zealand tax nexus: a foreign-incorporated International Company (IC) must obtain a New Zealand IRD number if it derives New Zealand-sourced income, carries on a taxable activity in New Zealand, or supplies remote or digital services (including cross-border merchant acquiring, clearing and payment gateway services) to New Zealand-resident consumers or businesses; a pure offshore tax-exempt IC with no New Zealand nexus requires no New Zealand registration. Step 2 — Apply for the statutory TIN (IRD number): submit the Inland Revenue 'Non-resident company registration' application (form IR742, or the online application through myIR), attaching the Certificate of Incorporation, memorandum and articles of association, directors' and shareholders' registers, the ultimate beneficial ownership structure, the contract with the acquiring bank and card schemes, and a board resolution recording that central management and control is exercised outside New Zealand. Step 3 — Register for goods and services tax (GST): file the GST registration application in myIR selecting the taxable activity category for financial services/payment processing, entering the actual or expected 12-month taxable supplies, and choosing the monthly or two-monthly tax period; non-resident suppliers of remote services must use the dedicated non-resident service supplier registration track and nominate an address for service in New Zealand and, if required, a New Zealand tax agent. Step 4 — Obtain ancillary statutory identifiers: if the IC establishes a New Zealand branch or registered place of business, register as an overseas company on the New Zealand Companies Register and obtain a New Zealand Business Number (NZBN); concurrently register as a Financial Service Provider on the Financial Service Providers Register (FSPR) and as a reporting entity under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 with the Department of Internal Affairs, which are statutory licensing prerequisites for the Visa/Mastercard direct acquiring and Fedwire clearing rails. Step 5 — Evidence the tax-exempt classification: retain the IC's home-jurisdiction tax exemption certificate, annual return and the offshore International Companies Act registration record so that Inland Revenue accepts the Tax_Exempt_Zone status for income tax purposes and applies GST only to New Zealand-targeted supplies; because the IC's residence jurisdiction does not maintain a double tax agreement with New Zealand, reliance is placed exclusively on the domestic non-resident sourcing rules in the Income Tax Act 2007 and the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985 to limit New Zealand exposure to New Zealand-sourced income and New Zealand-resident consumer supplies.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: New Zealand does not administer a United States-style check-the-box election; entity classification follows the substantive form under the Companies Act 1993, the Income Tax Act 2007 and the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985. The available statutory elections and alignment mechanisms for the IC payment gateway structure are: (1) voluntary GST registration (GST Act 1985 s 51) for supplies below the NZD 60,000 threshold; (2) GST group registration (GST Act 1985 s 55) enabling the IC and any New Zealand branch or associated gateway entity to file a single consolidated GST return; (3) the non-resident remote services simplified registration and return regime under the GST Act 1985 (applicable to offshore suppliers of electronic services) with an election to zero-rate business-to-business supplies made to New Zealand GST-registered recipients; (4) the Look-Through Company (LTC) election under Income Tax Act 2007 ss HA 4-HA 6, available only to closely held New Zealand-resident companies and therefore unavailable to the non-resident IC unless the IC becomes managed and controlled in New Zealand, in which case entity-level taxation at 28% is the default; (5) the financial services input tax attribution election and de minimis threshold under GST Act 1985 s 20(3H) and s 20C, which affects the recoverability of GST on acquired services where the IC also supplies exempt domestic financial services; (6) the hybrid mismatch and cross-border alignment rules under Income Tax Act 2007 part FH, which require the IC to file a hybrid mismatch disposition notice where deduction/non-inclusion outcomes would otherwise arise; and (7) the branch equivalent method option under the transfer pricing rules for any New Zealand permanent establishment.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Reserve Bank of New Zealand (Te Pūtea Matua), with the Financial Markets Authority as conduct regulator for financial services and the Department of Internal Affairs as AML/CFT supervisor for payment service providers.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The New Zealand dollar (NZD) is freely convertible for both current account and capital account transactions. New Zealand maintains no exchange controls, no quantitative restrictions, and no prior approval requirements on cross-border fund transfers, consistent with its Article VIII IMF obligations under the Bretton Woods system. Profit remittances, dividends, and capital repatriation to non-resident shareholders are unrestricted from a banking and foreign-exchange perspective; the only statutory constraints are the imposition of architecture non-resident withholding tax on dividends and the Overseas Investment Act 2005, which applies exclusively to certain sensitive land or significant business assets. The International Company and its cross-border payment gateway operation may freely hold multi-currency accounts, contract foreign currency settlements, and transfer funds offshore without Reserve Bank consent or conversion mandates.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: New Zealand imposes no export-proceeds surrender timeline and no mandatory conversion ratio. Exporters, licensed payment service providers, and online merchant acquirers may retain 100% of foreign currency receipts without repatriation obligation, maintain nostro and wallet balances in any freely convertible currency, and execute offshore settlements directly through authorized financial institutions or registered clearing channels. Cross-border earnings from acquiring services are treated as ordinary business receipts and are subject only to standard corporate income-tax measurement and source-category characterization under New Zealand domestic law, not to any foreign-exchange custody or surrender regime.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore digital electronic-money institutions (EMIs) within the target payment gateway model carry a Medium viability rating. Registration as a Financial Service Provider under the Financial Service Providers (Registration and Dispute Resolution) Act 2008 is mandatory, and a New Zealand resident agent is required for foreign-owned entities conducting regulated financial services. Direct membership of the Reserve Bank of New Zealand Exchange Settlement Account System (ESAS) is legally limited to registered banks, so an offshore EMI without a New Zealand banking booking entity must clear through a tier-1 domestic bank sponsor or obtain a Department of Internal Affairs reporting-entity designation under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009. The practical constraints include the absence of passported EMI licensing privileges from OECD or EU home states, reinforced capital-adequacy expectations from sponsoring banks, and the requirement to maintain segregated statutory trust accounts for merchant funds.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: A physical-presence mandate applies to the ultimate beneficial owner and at least one executive director of the International Company. Tier-1 New Zealand banks require an in-person or notarized video-verified due-diligence interview for structures classified as high-risk PSPs in the merchant-acquiring sector. Remote onboarding is available only where the entity already holds a New Zealand FSP license, is registered as an AML/CFT reporting entity with the Department of Internal Affairs, and furnishes apostilled corporate resolutions, a certificate of incumbency, and signed declarations of beneficial ownership. Recommended practice is the physical attendance of the director for the statutory onboarding interview at either the Auckland or Wellington corporate banking branch, combined with contemporaneous verification of the passport, proof of residential address, and electronic signature capture.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk PSP classification and the absence of a New Zealand statutory operating license
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Regulatory pack comprising the valid Financial Service Provider certificate, Department of Internal Affairs reporting-entity registration confirmation, Visa and Mastercard principal or sub-member acquiring agreements, an AML/CFT compliance programme approved by a qualified AML/CFT compliance officer, audited financial statements for two fiscal years, and a treasury flow map demonstrating segregation of client funds in statutory trust accounts.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opacity in non-resident beneficial ownership and layered trust structure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Trust deed summary, register of significant persons capturing all holders of 25% or greater economic interest, source-of-wealth and source-of-funds letters, professional legal reference from a New Zealand-licensed barrister or solicitor, apostilled certificate of good standing from the incorporation jurisdiction, and sworn declarations identifying each settlor, trustee, protector, and beneficiary.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border wire-transparency alerts under the AML/CFT Act 2009 and the AML/CFT (Wire Transfer) Regulations 2012
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full originator and beneficiary information embedded in every SWIFT MT103 message, including legal name, physical address, legal entity identifier or passport number, and account number; correspondent-banking due-diligence questionnaire; automated sanctions-screening policy updated daily for NZ, OFAC, EU, and UN lists; and an independent assurance letter confirming elimination of anonymous and third-party intermediary wires.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unexpected transaction velocity and concentrated merchant counterparty exposure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Merchant underwriting and termination policy, daily transaction monitoring thresholds calibrated to the acquiring portfolio, PCI-DSS Level 1 attestation of compliance, chargeback and refund reserve ledger, quarterly cash-flow forecasting aligned with escrow balances, and bank-comfort letters evidencing the completed know-your-customer clearance of the top ten merchant counterparties.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity or subordinated shareholder funding is executed through SWIFT MT103 or MT202 credit transfers with the payment narrative expressly stating the transaction as 'direct investment in cross-border payment gateway operations' or 'intercompany financing for merchant settlement capital', and the receiving bank mapping the transaction to the appropriate Balance of Payments direct-investment classification for New Zealand statutory reporting. The banking protocol requires an apostilled board resolution approving the capital injection, source-of-funds clearance through the treasury compliance team, and credit only to a designated capital escrow account at ANZ Bank New Zealand Limited or Bank of New Zealand following positive match on the beneficial-ownership register.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound merchant settlements and trade disbursements are cleared through three parallel rails: SWIFT MT103 for high-value international credit transfers and supplier settlements; commercial letters of credit at sight for goods-based merchant imports and trade-finance transactions; and Visa and Mastercard direct settlement rails for acquiring-payout obligations to downstream merchants. All outbound credit transfers are batched and pre-funded through a dedicated operational clearing account maintained with a tier-1 domestic settlement bank to eliminate intraday liquidity gaps within the Exchange Settlement Account System window. Each outgoing transaction embeds full originator information, unique transaction reference, merchant identity code, and settlement-currency instruction to support audit trails and chargeback management.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable NZD/USD spot and vanilla forward contracts with a maximum tenor of 12 months
Cross-currency swaps involving NZD/USD, NZD/EUR, and NZD/AUD for structural settlement hedging
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) restricted exclusively to illiquid emerging-market currencies arising from the merchant acquiring portfolio
European-style FX options (puts and calls) for downside protection on projected settlement fee receivables
Intercompany currency netting arrangements between the New Zealand treasury centre and affiliated acquiring entities, executed under documented bilateral master agreements

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Financial Supervisory Commission (FSC), Rarotonga, Cook Islands
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one calendar month after each anniversary of incorporation (the annual 'return date'); a substituted return date is available with Registrar approval; filing is effected electronically by the licensed registered agent.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Statutory daily default penalty (NZD 50 per day of continued default under Section 74 of the Act); if the annual return and government fee remain unpaid for more than six months, the Registrar may publish a strike-off notice in the Cook Islands Gazette and remove the company from the International Companies Register. The company is then dissolved and its assets vest in the Crown; restoration requires an application to the High Court of the Cook Islands.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual PSP License Renewal and Compliance Return (Financial Services Development Act 2019)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Commission (FSC) of the Cook Islands, Licensing Division
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on or before the license anniversary (specified in the FSC license instrument; typically 31 December); audited financial statements must accompany the compliance return within six months of the company's financial year end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-renewal automatically suspends the payment service license; the FSC may revoke the license after 21 days' written notice. Carrying on regulated payment activities without a valid license is an offence under the Financial Services Development Act 2019 punishable by fines up to NZD 100,000 and possible administrative strike-off of the company.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Ownership (UBO) Confirmation / Register Update
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Commission (FSC) of the Cook Islands, Registries Division (submitted through the licensed registered agent)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filed concurrently with the Annual Return within one month of the incorporation anniversary; share transfers or beneficial ownership changes occurring during the year must be notified to the registered agent within 14 days and the UBO register amended within 21 days of each change.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Contravention of the beneficial ownership obligations constitutes an offence punishable by fines of up to NZD 20,000 per breach; additionally, the FSC may issue compliance directions, suspend the filing privileges of the registered agent, and ultimately strike the company off the International Companies Register.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit is imposed on: (a) all financial services licensees of the FSC, including the licensed cross-border payment gateway PSP, irrespective of size; and (b) any other international company satisfying two or more of the large-company criteria across two consecutive accounting periods: total assets above NZD 60 million, gross annual revenue above NZD 30 million, or 50 or more full-time employees.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: New Zealand Equivalents to International Financial Reporting Standards (NZ IFRS) as adopted in the Cook Islands; the FSC permits licensed international companies to present financial statements under IFRS as issued by the IASB.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The company must maintain a confidential Register of Beneficial Owners (UBO register) at its registered office and file an annual beneficial ownership confirmation with the FSC Registrar simultaneously with the statutory annual return. The confirmation must identify all individuals with significant control, declare any shares issued or transferred during the reporting year, and be certified by a director and the licensed registered agent. Changes in beneficial ownership must be notified to the registered agent within 14 days, and the UBO register and FSC confirmation updated within 21 days of any such change.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,200 - USD 3,000 per annum for licensed Cook Islands registered agent services covering registered office, agent representation, statutory register maintenance, and annual return preparation/filing
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 8,000 - USD 15,000 per annum for a licensed cross-border payment gateway international company, depending on transaction volume, number of bank accounts, and audit complexity (includes financial statement preparation under NZ IFRS/IFRS and the independent auditor's report)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% for the CK_IC as a Cook Islands International Company under the tax-exempt international company regime; 20% statutory Cook Islands corporate rate if the exemption is broken for local-source income; 28% New Zealand corporate rate if central management and control is recharacterised to New Zealand.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Statutory 100% exemption on all non-Cook Islands-source income; no corporate income tax on cross-border payment gateway fees; no New Zealand tax while the company remains non-resident and has no New Zealand permanent establishment; no capital gains tax on disposal of foreign investments; no dividend withholding tax on distributions to non-resident shareholders; no stamp duty on international company transactions; annual government fee is the only routine fiscal impost.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Cook Islands International Company Annual Return filed with the Registrar of International Companies through the Cook Islands Financial Supervisory Commission online registry; no statutory income tax return is otherwise due while the IC exemption applies.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 6 months after the anniversary of incorporation; annual government fee payable by the anniversary date.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name and unique International Company registration number.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the exact name and registration number from the certificate of incorporation; do not use a New Zealand company IRD number.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registered office address in the Cook Islands.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Must be the office of the registered agent in Rarotonga; a post office box or virtual office is not acceptable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Principal business address, including any payment processing or merchant acquiring operations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a non-resident IC, state the foreign head office outside the Cook Islands; avoid reciting a New Zealand management address if the company is claiming non-residence.
Include non-resident directors; board minutes must show decisions made outside New Zealand to avoid NZ central management and control.
Nominee shareholders must disclose underlying beneficial ownership; false beneficial ownership declarations invoke AML and fraud liabilities.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration that no local business is carried on in the Cook Islands.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident ICs must certify that no taxable local activity is undertaken; administrative formalities and registered agent functions do not constitute local business.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Economic substance declaration, particularly for a relevant payment services activity.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Confirm where the core income-generating activities are performed and directed; a shell IC with a full underwriting contract but no Cook Islands employees is a red flag.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Annual fee calculation and payment confirmation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Pay in New Zealand dollars from a non-New Zealand bank account where possible; the annual fee is not an income tax and does not confer New Zealand tax residence.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late annual return: additional penalty of NZD 100 per month or part month and possible strike-off after six months; failure to file is an offence under the International Companies Act 2011-12 carrying fines up to NZD 5,000; if the Registrar strikes off the company, assets vest in the Crown and directors may be disqualified.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: New Zealand IR4 Company Income Tax Return filed through IRD myIR or approved e-filing channel; this return is compulsory only if the CK_IC is recharacterised as a New Zealand tax resident or has a New Zealand permanent establishment.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a standard 31 March balance date, the IR4 must be filed by 7 July following year-end when e-filed; non-standard balance dates are due no later than the last day of the fourth month after balance date.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the company is inadvertently NZ-resident, declare worldwide payment gateway revenue; if non-resident with a PE, declare only New Zealand-source income attributable to the PE.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible expenses attributable to the income returned.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Allocate arm's-length costs to the New Zealand PE; do not deduct head office overheads except under NZ transfer pricing rules.

Non-resident companies generally cannot maintain a New Zealand imputation credit account unless they elect into the NZ tax system; foreign withholding tax credits may be claimed only under double tax agreements.
Claim Cook Islands tax credits only for actual tax paid, not for the exempt international company fee; a zero-rate exemption generates no creditable foreign tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Transfer pricing adjustments on cross-border related-party payments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose all payment gateway licensing, processing, merchant acquiring, and management fees paid to related offshore entities; use CUP or TNMM with contemporaneous documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Australian resident or New Zealand resident status and PE declaration.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A foreign IC whose board meets in New Zealand will be treated as resident; a payment gateway may also create a fixed place based on a server only if it constitutes an enterprise permanent establishment under the DTA.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of NZD 250 initial, then NZD 50 per day up to NZD 5,000; late payment triggers interest and an automatic 10% late tax payment penalty; shortfall penalties may reach 150% of the avoided tax in cases of abusive tax avoidance.
